verdicts.evidence: Wrote and ran a throwaway adversarial script (cd .../community-traces-reconcile-latency && PYTHONPATH= .venv/bin/python - <<EOF). v1 of the harness reported FAILs, but I traced every one to a HARNESS flaw, not an R5 break: v1 rebuilt two INDEPENDENT git repos which got different commit timestamps -> different commit SHAs, and commit_id.hex is part of the anchor payload, so the content_hash trivially differed. (Also tp5-A normalized to tp5-a via normalize_id, agreeing across both paths.) v2 fixed this by building ONE repo+event-log to a pre-reconcile state, then making byte-identical filesystem clones (shutil.copytree -> same git objects/refs/event log/commit SHA) and running each reconciler on a clone. The legacy comparator is an INDEPENDENT per-patch reconcile that actually WRITES one git_anchor_search_completed event per patch (old shape) plus per-match anchors, reusing only the impl matchers (so only the anchor SET is under test). Result with corrected harness: ALL 6 scenarios PASS, anchor payload SET byte-identical new-vs-legacy. Extra probes: PROBE A confirmed observed_ref is honestly in the hash and identical across paths when called identically (post-commit hook always passes a resolved SHA; R5 only requires new-called-like-old == old); PROBE B (R7 mixed log) pre-seeded tpB-0 as a LEGACY per-patch anchor then ran the new reconcile: legacy-seeded hash present in pure-new set, new reconcile correctly skipped tpB-0 and re-anchored only tpB-1/tpB-2, mixed-log anchor SET == pure-new SET, read_events(verify=True) passed. Test suites: tests/core/test_reconcile_recording.py + tests/cli/test_trail_delayed_anchor.py = 20 passed; broader -k 'search_records or maturation or anchor or reconcile or trail_explain or trail_query or iter_search' = 91 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed.
verdicts.notes: No R5 divergence found; the invariant holds. All apparent divergences in my first harness pass were harness artifacts (independent repos producing different commit SHAs inside the payload, plus the expected normalize_id lowercasing), explicitly excluded by the task ('event_id/event_sequence differences are EXPECTED and NOT a failure' — different commit SHAs are an even more obvious harness artifact). The reason R5 holds structurally: the git_anchor_created drafts in the new reconcile (anchors.py:301-314) are built from the IDENTICAL matcher (_find_exact_anchor/_find_structural_anchor) and the IDENTICAL anchor_payload construction (anchors.py:265-281) as before; the ONLY change is collapsing N per-patch git_anchor_search_completed events into ONE v2 summary event. The dedup keys (existing_anchor_keys per-(patch,commit); existing_search_keys per-(patch,commit,attribution_version) fanned through iter_search_records) reproduce the legacy per-patch dedup semantics exactly, which is why late-patch, idempotent, attribution-bump, and attach-scope all match. Caveat on the legacy comparator: it is my reconstruction of pre-plan-090 semantics (the actual old code is not in the worktree), so 'legacy' = a faithful per-patch reimplementation reusing the impl matchers, not the literal historical function; this is the correct surface to test since R5 is about the anchor PAYLOAD set, and the payload construction is shared code that I exercised directly. Pre-existing, plan-090-unrelated env issue: tests/perf/* and tests/test_hatch_build.py fail at COLLECTION (missing 'textual'/'hatchling' optional dev deps); these error before any test body runs and are not in scope for R5.

verdicts.evidence:
Confirmed clean imports: `PYTHONPATH= .venv/bin/python -c "import opentraces; from opentraces.core.trails import iter_search_records, summary_search_touches_trace, is_summary_search_event"` succeeds. Ran focused + broad suites: test_reconcile_recording.py (6 passed), the 5 modified test files (46 passed), full-stack-demo + corpus integration (4 passed), corpus --check OK (34 files), trace-index perf/cheap-sync (17 passed), test_trail_explain.py + test_trail_reconciler.py (24 passed), and a broad trail/bucket/workspace/maturation/reconcile sweep (124 passed, 379 deselected).

Hunt result: searched the whole src tree for `event.trace_id ==`, `.trace_id ==`, `payload.get("trace_id")`, per-trace read_events loops, and direct per-patch payload reads on git_anchor_search_completed (`payload['result']`, `payload['trace_patch_id']`, `payload['created_anchor_ids']`, `payload['algorithms_attempted']`). Examined every hit. The two already-fixed fan-in surfaces are correct: bucket_store.py:1390 (per-trace trail.jsonl.gz companion, `summary_search_touches_trace`) and workspace.py:337 (`_trace_events` -> export/timeline). No OTHER unfanned-in per-trace surface exists.

Why every other candidate is NOT a drop:
- explain.py: explain_commit (the one migrated) uses iter_search_records gated on top-level search_head (line 254-261). explain_trace_step (NOT migrated) is fine because a searched patch's step always hits the patch branch whose source_events come from snapshots+patch+git_anchor_created only (lines 145-160) — search events were never surfaced there even in legacy. The no-patch branch (line 115) can't contain a search event (search implies a patch). The _source_event special-case at explain.py:22-24 is never reached with a summary.
- query.py: search_events_by_patch built via iter_search_records (line 322-326); _source_event (line 44-46 special-case) only ever called on patch_event/anchor_event (lines 373, 489), never a summary. Dead-but-unreached special-case.
- anchors.py dedup (196-205) and read_events_scoped commit_filter (event_log.py:606-609) both key on top-level search_head.hex, preserved verbatim in v2 — mixed-log dedup correct.
- Filtered-by-other-event-type-first (summary never touched): ingest.py:866-872, bursts.py:1384-1395, reconciler.py:261-296 + _patch_matches_window, snapshots.py:1003-1014, resources.py:_index_events:123-137 + _resolve_trace_patch_trail_by_id:356-364, rebuild.py:94-112, supersede.py:56-71, cli/trail.py:106-117/152-163, cli/doctor.py:82-90 (skips trace_id=None, counts only file_edit/patch), trail.py:_audit_trail_capture:211-217 (counts only file_edit/patch), workspace.py snapshot fns (152/205/1008).
- Not event-log readers: inverse_blame.py:113 (TraceRecord), datasets.py:674 (bucket objects), trace_meta.py, graph_renderer.py, web/server.py, attribution.py/atif.py/agent_trace.py/publish.py (TraceRecord/snapshots).
- Other read_events loops verified harmless: build_survival_cache_index (CACHED_SURVIVAL_EVENT_TYPE only), context_tree/query.py:355-362 (context-tree event types only), bucket_store.py:494 (events mirror, no trace filter, verbatim), bucket_store.py:1228-1237 (timestamps only, no trace filter), trace_index.py:1516 (survival cache only), installers.py:2371 (LLM-review results, unrelated), workspace.py _source_event:119-124 (envelope-only, no payload access, safe on summary).
verdicts.notes:
Two non-blocking observations (both defensible by construction, no action required):

1. _trace_ids_for_project (bucket_store.py:1613-1635) — the bucket-projection trace enumerator — does NOT fan summaries in: it collects `event.trace_id` (+ payload fallback), so a summary (trace_id=None) contributes nothing. This is SAFE because every trace_id appearing in a summary's results[] necessarily also has a `trace_patch_created` event carrying that real trace_id (a search only happens for an existing patch; anchors.py:206-211 sources results from patch_event.trace_id). So no trace is ever known ONLY via a summary. Worth a one-line comment noting the invariant, but not a bug. Same reasoning covers the duplicate enumerator at bucket_store.py:1629-1635.

2. timeline/play row-count delta (workspace.py play_trace_timeline -> _timeline_entry) — in legacy, N per-patch search rows appeared per trace with trace_id/step_index set; now ONE summary row appears with trace_id=null/step_index=null and no per-patch breakdown. This is the documented contract delta (the summary shares one event_id across patches) and is already reflected in the updated corpus fixtures (trail_play.json, opened_trail_play.json, trail_events.jsonl) — corpus --check is green. _timeline_entry never surfaced per-patch search payload even in legacy (it only used envelope fields for search events), so no field-level data is silently lost; it is purely a row-count change, expected under R4.

Net: Approach A' is fully fanned-in. The only two per-trace consumers that needed fan-in (bucket companion + workspace export/timeline) are correctly handled via summary_search_touches_trace; all other search-result consumers go through iter_search_records or never see search events. No blocking_issues.

The mixed-log reality is sound: the validator (_reject_bare_git_object_ids in models.py walks the whole payload rejecting any GIT_SHA_RE string under a *_sha key or BARE_GIT_SHA_KEYS) is why the summary keeps commit identity only in the top-level search_head {algo,hex} and the results[] entries avoid *_sha keys — verified that both the v2 summary and a hand-built legacy per-patch event pass model_validate. The append-only contract holds: import round-trip preserves every event_id including the summary's, so the ~505K legacy events already on live logs are never rewritten and continue to be read via iter_search_records alongside new summary events. One observation (not a defect): the documented contract delta that a v2 summary's per-patch records share one event_id/event_sequence/event_time is intentional and visible in explain_commit source_events (one source_event per searched patch, sharing the summary's event_id). My initial secondary probe asserted tp-legacy would be anchored in C1, which was my own mistaken expectation — the hand-rolled legacy event recorded result=unknown with no git_anchor_created, so C1 correctly has zero anchored trace_patches; the load-bearing leak check (tp-a NOT anchored in C1) passed.
